text.p: An oddly banked track squeezed inside the Bercy stadium will deprive the world indoor championships of fast 200 and 400 metres times, leading British runner Jamie Baulch lamented on Friday.

"It's a bit of a shame that maybe you won't see the times in the 200s and 400s that you would have seen on faster tracks," Baulch said after clocking 46.52 seconds in the opening round of the 400 metres on the first day of the three-day competition.
The time was more than 1.2 seconds off his year's leading time. Bonuses of $50,000 for world records are being paid here for the first time at a world championships.
"The second bend on the first flat is quite tight,and it threw me off a bit," Baulch said.
British women's 400 metres runner Phylis Smith added: "It's a horrible track, it's terrible. Everyone is complaining about it."
Trinidad's Ato Boldon, favourite for the men's 200 title, also complained.
"It's not particularly fast," said Boldon. "It has no bounce. It's flat."
The configuration of the track upset Smith the most.

"Normally I would accelerate after the bend, but you can't do that because as soon as you try that you go really wide...it pushes you over into the next lane," she said. "It's like running in a gully."
The track was also uneven, prompting some athletes to worry about falling, Smith said.
She said lane one was more than a centimetre higher than the other lanes.
"It's a fast track," Smith said, "but if it was more like Birmingham they would probably have more records broken."
There were also complaints about both the starter and the gun by American Olympic 100 metres champion Gail Devers.
"He's a very quick starter," she said. "There's hardly time to get set. The gun is odd, it doesn't sound like a gun."
